summary: Master 3d atomic and ionic radii trends, effective nuclear charge balance, and second/third ionization enthalpy anomalies.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.1 Atomic & Ionic Radii Profiles
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.1 Atomic & Ionic Radii Profiles

summaryBox.title: 3d Radii Variations
summaryBox.takeaway: Sc ──► Cr radii decrease; Mn ──► Ni radii remain nearly flat; Cu ──► Zn radii expand slightly due to d¹⁰ electron-electron repulsion.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
$3d$ SERIES ATOMIC RADII TREND
                      
   $\text{Sc} \rightarrow \text{Cr}$: Radii **DECREASE** (Increasing $Z_{\text{eff}}$ overrides $3d$ shielding).
   $\text{Mn} \rightarrow \text{Ni}$: Radii **REMAIN NEARLY FLAT** ($3d$ electron shielding balances increasing $Z$).
   $\text{Cu} \rightarrow \text{Zn}$: Radii **INCREASE SLIGHTLY** ($3d^{10}$ inter-electronic repulsions expand lattice).
conceptBreakdown.content:
Across the 3d transition series, atomic and ionic radii display three distinct regimes:
1. **$\text{Sc} \rightarrow \text{Cr}$**: Atomic radius decreases rapidly because increasing nuclear charge ($Z_{\text{eff}}$) pulls the outer electrons inward, overcoming the screening effect of added 3d electrons.
2. **$\text{Mn} \rightarrow \text{Ni}$**: Atomic radius remains almost constant because the screening effect of 3d electrons almost exactly balances the increase in nuclear charge.
3. **$\text{Cu} \rightarrow \text{Zn}$**: Atomic radius increases slightly because paired $3d^{10}$ electrons create strong inter-electronic repulsions that expand the electron cloud.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.2 Ionization Enthalpy (Δ_i H) Irregularities
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.2 Ionization Enthalpy (Δ_i H) Irregularities
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
SUCCESSIVE IONIZATION ANOMALIES
                       
   $\mathbf{\Delta_i H_2 \text{ Anomaly (Cr and Cu):}}$
   ├── $\text{Cr}^+ (3d^5) \rightarrow \text{Cr}^{2+} (3d^4)$: Unusually HIGH $\Delta_i H_2$ (Breaks stable half-filled $3d^5$).
   └── $\text{Cu}^+ (3d^{10}) \rightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+} (3d^9)$: Unusually HIGH $\Delta_i H_2$ (Breaks stable $3d^{10}$).
   
   $\mathbf{\Delta_i H_3 \text{ Anomaly (Mn and Zn):}}$
   ├── $\text{Mn}^{2+} (3d^5) \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{3+} (3d^4)$: Unusually HIGH $\Delta_i H_3$ (Breaks stable half-filled $3d^5$).
   └── $\text{Zn}^{2+} (3d^{10}) \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{3+} (3d^9)$: Unusually HIGH $\Delta_i H_3$ (Breaks stable fully-filled $3d^{10}$).
conceptBreakdown.content:
Across the 3d series, $\Delta_i H_1$ increases gradually, but displays specific anomalies in $\Delta_i H_2$ and $\Delta_i H_3$ due to the removal of electrons from stable configurations:
- **$\Delta_i H_2$ High**: $\text{Cr}^+$ ($3d^5$) and $\text{Cu}^+$ ($3d^{10}$).
- **$\Delta_i H_3$ High**: $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ($3d^5$) and $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ ($3d^{10}$).

Δ_i H_2 is exceptionally high for Cr and Cu (disrupts 3d⁵ and 3d¹⁰).
Δ_i H_3 is exceptionally high for Mn and Zn (disrupts 3d⁵ and 3d¹⁰).
